Question: What are the signs that my Amazon bird's pin feathers are ready to be preened?
Answer: If the feather sheathe is transparent they are generally ready to be preened, but what I do is apply gentle pressure with the pads of my finger and thumb first. If the sheathe “cracks,” it’s ready, if it is soft, it’s not.

Name: Mercedes R. Lackey
Question: “If you work hard, you’ll be successful in life” To what extent do you agree with this statement?
Answer: Normally I don’t supply content for anyone else’s space but this statement is such an unmitigated crock of bullshit I had to post. I know people who work two and three jobs just to have enough money to keep a roof over their heads. They are working hard, very hard, certainly harder than the kinds of people who spout this bullshit, but they are not successful by any measure. I also know trust-fund babies who don’t work at all, not one bit. Someone else does all the work for them. Zero work, but counted as very successful. As near as I can figure out, this sort of statement is put out by the second sorts of people to keep the first sorts in line. To shame them into thinking, “Well, this person is very successful and this is what they say, so I must not be working hard enough.” It’s also put out by supervisors or bosses to keep the drudges in line, to blame and shame them for something they can do nothing about. In all cases it’s bullshit. How hard you work has very little correlation with success in life. Only the right combination of education, skills, and opportunity combined with hard work can make you successful. It’s the four legs of a table; lose one and the table falls over.
